html:
Cyclone Pam, one of the strongest storms recorded in the South Pacific, struck Vanuatu on 13 March 2015. It destroyed or damaged most buildings in the capital, Port Vila, and on the southern islands.

Gardens and crops were flattened across the country, and food aid was needed for months. The death toll was kept low by warnings and by people sheltering in strong buildings, but the damage equalled most of a year's national income.

Vanuatu's president spoke out at a United Nations meeting on disasters held that same week, linking the storm to climate change. It was followed by Cyclone Winston in Fiji a year later. See also Port Vila.
sum: Cyclone Pam, one of the strongest storms recorded in the South Pacific, struck Vanuatu on 13 March 2015. It destroyed or damaged most buildings in the capital, Port Vila, and on the southern islands.
